[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The self-managed worker Auto Scaling group :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.workers can launch instances as soon as its launch configuration is available, but its role-policy attachments are not dependencies. It should wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy so nodes do not start before their worker permissions are attached.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
`:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.workers` can launch instances before `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy` is attached, so nodes may start without the permissions needed to join the EKS cluster. Ensure the worker group waits for this attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The worker Auto Scaling group can launch instances as soon as it is created, but it has no ordering dependency on the worker-node policy attachment. Ensure the policy is attached before launching worker instances.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_autoscaling_group.workers launches EC2 instances that use aws_iam_role.workers, but there is no attribute reference or depends_on ordering it after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy (nor the CNI/ECR attachments). If the ASG is created and starts launching instances before the worker role's policies are attached, the nodes boot with a role lacking the required EKS policies and fail to join/operate until IAM propagation catches up. The module already protects the managed node_groups path against exactly this race via the data.null_data_source.node_groups ordering hack (its inputs include the three policy attachment IDs), but the launch-configuration worker group has no equivalent guard. A bare depends_on covering the three worker policy attachments closes the gap; there is no clean data reference on the ASG that would express it.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
EKS will not admit worker nodes whose IAM role lacks AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy. The ASG and aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy are parallel branches off aws_iam_role.workers with no ordering between them, so nodes could be provisioned before the policy is attached and fail to join the cluster. The null_data_source.node_groups hack covers module.node_groups but not this self-managed ASG; an explicit depends_on is needed since no ASG attribute can reference the attachment.
